_source: Our own table: the recipes of UEV's Barnard b (docs/eras/uev.md, machines 21 and 22; lines 10 and 15; package UEV-B3). Real practice behind each step: coring rigs on metal-rich crust, the Mond process (Vale's Clydach refinery: nickel carbonyl; BASF's carbonyl iron powder), aqua regia digestion of platinum-group residues, and the recovery of rhenium as ammonium perrhenate, recrystallised and reduced with hydrogen (Rheniumnickel, Climax Molybdenum plants).
_how_it_is_used: Read by server_scripts/grindless/uev/barnard.js at every server load. Each entry becomes one recipe of its type, id grindless:<type>/<name> (GTM's builder puts the type in front); carbonyl_refining carries the data key of the type = <name> (the EMI line). barnard_core_drilling is the drill's own type (data key grindless_barnard_core_drilling).

site 'barnard_b': the recipe runs only on grindless:barnard_b (G.places). Every recipe of this table has it: Barnard rock, the carbonyls and every rhenium producer (offworld_only.json's 'barnard' row watches gtceu:rhenium*) are Barnard b's.
items in and out: { id, count, chance? } (chance in 1/10,000; below 10,000 a chanced input or output of 1); kept: items not used up; fluid lists: { id, amount } in mB.

One recipe per lookup path: the circuit is the step on carbonyl_refining; the drill's two recipes differ by the survey (kept) against the circuit; no recipe of a type takes a subset of another's ingredients (checked at load; the pilot core's circuit 1 keeps it apart from the survey recipe).

Bootstrap: the drill's survey (A8, tables/earth_orbit.json: grindless:barnard_gravity_survey, circuit 2) is made from 4 Barnard core rock, and the rock comes from this drill. So circuit 1 of the drill, with the bit only, cores a small pilot (2 rock, no survey, programmed circuit 1); with the survey the drill cores 8 rock a run (the survey is kept) and needs no circuit. Both wear the bit 5 % a run.

CO: the refinery takes 5,000 mB of CO per 1,000 mB of Fe(CO)5, and A5's nitride works (tables/composites.json, carbonyl_iron_powder) gives the same 5,000 mB of CO back; the HV syngas plant's CO-rich row (circuit 6, C + CO2 -> 2 CO) makes the CO. Nickel and cobalt carbonyls are formed and cracked inside the vessel (contained): CO nets to zero there.

Destinations: the residue goes to EV's platinum plant (circuit 9, server_scripts/grindless/ev/platinum_plant.js: Os, Ir and Pt dust and tungsten dust come out, the rhenium as crude ammonium perrhenate), the nickel and cobalt to the network's stock, the ammonia of the reduction back to the platinum plant's digest, the ammonium chloride of the recrystallisation to GTM's ammonia loop, the water to the network's water.

Rhenium: gtceu:rhenium_dust is made only here (reduction row), and gtceu:rhenium_ingot only from the pellet; GTM's own smelting route (dust -> ingot in a furnace) is not needed: the pellet is sintered in a hydrogen atmosphere in the electric blast furnace (2700 K, about 80 % of rhenium's melting point, tune; GTM gives rhenium no blast recipe of its own; the hydrogen is used up keeping the oxide out). The electron beam's rhenium row (2 ingots -> 2 grindless:six_n_rhenium, A4) take them on from there.

recipes._why: MAX-R1 (max.md, L13 step 2, c2): the belt bloom carbonylated in CO; the Fe and Ni carbonyls are formed and cracked inside the vessel, so the CO returns whole (contained, nets to zero).
